name: Occupational health and pre-employment medicals
summary: How expats book pre-employment, EP issuance, and workplace medicals in Singapore — what MOM/employer panels actually need, vs executive screens sold as “medical check” upsells.
body:
Not every “health screening” satisfies an Employment Pass issuance exam, offshore fitness certificate, or employer onboarding panel. Occupational health clinics and designated GP/panel labs exist to match form fields — chest X-ray, HIV, pregnancy where required, vision, and role-specific tests.

## Common triggers
- EP / S Pass issuance medical after in-principle approval
- Pre-employment forms for finance, healthcare, education, or F&B roles
- Offshore / shipyard / height fitness and audiometry
- Return-to-work or periodic surveillance for certain industries
- Driver or heavy-vehicle medicals when relevant

Bring the exact form PDF. Clinics cannot invent MOM fields from a wellness brochure.

## Choosing a clinic
Panel clinics familiar with MOM forms reduce rejection loops. Hospital executive suites can run thorough screens that still miss a single tick-box the employer needs. Ask whether results upload to the required portal or arrive as stamped hardcopy within your IPA window.

## Privacy and cost
Employer-paid medicals may share results with HR under consent — read what you sign. Self-paid issuance medicals are usually cash and modest compared with full-body packages. Do not buy tumour-marker add-ons to “speed” an EP medical.

## How to choose
Match clinic to form type, turnaround SLA, and X-ray on-site vs referral. For shift workers, ask about early slots. If you failed a prior film (old TB scar folklore), bring prior imaging so radiologists can compare.

## Practical tip
Book the medical as soon as IPA lands — peak weeks slip. Eat/fast only as instructed for that form; EP medicals are not always fasting lipid panels.
